title: rate-limit-spike-debug-journal
content:
Goal:
- Capture commands, exact responses, hypotheses and next steps while triaging a transient rate-limit/401 pattern affecting a small set of hosted-api customers. This is a scratchpad for fast iteration (notes-to-self style).

Timeline (local timestamps in PST):
- 2024-11-04 09:15: first alert from synthetic that /v1/generate returned 429 sporadically (3/100).
- 2024-11-04 09:18: Customer support ticket INC-2115 referencing 401 then immediate 429 when client retried.
- 2024-11-04 09:22: Started live capture on node-03 (region us-west2) and forwarded logs to Diego.

Commands tried (repro and diagnostics):
1) Simple curl repro against hosted API with bearer token used by affected customer:
   curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate" \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"gpt-lite-2","input":"hello"}'

   Response (example):
   HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   Retry-After: 3
   x-request-id: 4f9a7c2b
   x-rate-limit-limit: 120
   x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
   x-rate-limit-reset: 1700001120

   Notes: header values present. Remaining==0 even though account quota shows >0 in Console (possible quota partition mismatch).

2) Reproduce loop (10s interval) to capture intermittent 401->429 flip:
   for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s xreq:%{redirect_url}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX" https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate; sleep 1; done

   Observed sequence in one run: 200, 200, 401, 429, 429, 200, 200
   Hypothesis: token validation service timed out and returned 401, client retried quickly and hit rate-limiter while token revalidation in background.

3) Explicit token introspect against auth service (internal only):
   curl -X POST https://auth.internal.redwood/token/introspect -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-XXXXX" -d '' -i

   Example return when failing:
   HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
   x-request-id: a1b2c3d4

   When auth returns 504, our API returns 401 to the client (by design). Upstream retry behavior + lack of jitter could create burst of requests against rate limiter when tokens are revalidated.

SDK trace snippets (node client v0.12.3 local capture):
- [2024-11-04T09:21:12.345Z] request.start id=4f9a7c2b route=/v1/generate
- [2024-11-04T09:21:12.556Z] auth.cache.miss key=sk-cust-XXXXX
- [2024-11-04T09:21:13.009Z] auth.lookup.ok ttl=18s
- [2024-11-04T09:21:13.011Z] rate-limiter.consume remaining=0 window=60
- [2024-11-04T09:21:13.012Z] response 429 x-request-id=4f9a7c2b

Observed patterns and anomalies:
- Pattern A: 401 followed within <1s by 429s from the same client.
  Possible causes: transient auth outage leading to client retry flood OR auth latency causing some requests to bypass cached token checks while others are validated.
- Pattern B: x-rate-limit-remaining shows 0, but Console quota UI shows non-zero units. Potential mapping issue between product quota buckets and enforcement policy (e.g., project-level vs key-level counters).
- Pattern C: 429 Retry-After small integer (1-5s) but clients retry with no jitter, causing repeat 429s. No circuit-breaker in client.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Token validation service transient (504/502/timeout) causes API to return 401; client retries immediately and exhausts local per-key rate-limit bucket. The sequence looks like 401->retries->429. (Most likely)
2) A recent change to rate-limiter code switched enforcement from account-global counters to API-key-local counters for fraud mitigation; keys with many short-lived tokens now get double-counted. (medium)
3) Multiple backends (old proxy vs new gateway) have inconsistent header semantics (some set x-rate-limit headers differently), confusing monitoring and leading to mis-routed retries. (low)
4) Stale client SDK caches causing token mismatch and spurious 401s (individual customers only). (low-medium)

Immediate actionable checks (what I ran / next steps):
- Check auth-service metrics around 2024-11-04T09:15-09:30 for increased latency or 5xx spikes (done, small spike around 09:18).
- Correlate x-request-id from user response headers with gateway logs to trace backend path (in progress).
- Verify enforcement key for rate-limiter: is it key-id or account-id? Confirm mapping for the affected customer in Redis counters (Diego on it).
- Ask product: were there any recent config changes to quota bucket mappings? (PRIYA pinged)
- Add temporary increased logging on token-introspect path for that key (limited to 1h).
- Suggest change to client retry logic: exponential backoff + jitter and stop-after-5. Add to SDK backlog.

Repro snippets for QA (non-prod endpoint emulation):
- Emulate auth timeout then flood client: start a small auth proxy that responds 504 for N requests then 200. Then run the repro loop and confirm 401->429 sequence replicates. Script attached in linked artifact (github/infra-monitoring#34).

Longer-term mitigations to propose:
- Prefer returning 429 with Retry-After when token introspect is timing out (instead of 401) to avoid triggering client aggressive reauth/retry loops. Tradeoff: semantics change, needs product signoff.
- Rate-limiter: add short-lived grace window when auth cache refill is ongoing for a token to prevent double penalization.
- Improve SDK default retry policy to include jitter and respect Retry-After header.
- Dashboard: surface key-level counters vs account-level counters side-by-side to detect mapping issues quickly.

Notes to self (TODOs):
- [ ] Collect full traffic dump for node-03 between 09:12-09:28 (blocked by retention policy; escalate to SRE infra if needed).
- [ ] Confirm whether dedicated customers see same pattern (if not, more likely gateway config issue).
- [ ] Draft short how-to for support agents: "When customer reports 401 followed by 429, gather x-request-id, timestamp, sdk version, and last token rotation time."

Quick references (internal):
- Token introspect proto: confluence:auth/token-introspect (internal)
- Rate limiter config: confluence:infra/ratelimit-config

Free-form / random notes:
- Customer's client version: redwood-js-sdk@0.12.3 — check older SDKs for missing Retry-After handling.
- Observed one case where client rotated key mid-sequence (user-initiated rotation). Might explain 401 flank.
- Keep record of any correlation ids that map to external CDNs (fastly headers).

If stuck: escalate INFRA-721 to on-call for auth-service (Diego) and ask product for a temporary soft-fail policy on introspect path.

End of scratchpad.
